nl.statement: A cluster experiment with \(C\) mutually isolated sampled clusters of common size \(n\ge4\), a fixed menu \(\mathcal K=\{1,\ldots,K\}\) of \(2\le K\le n-1\) exact-count policies with distinct target treated counts \(1\le m_1<\cdots<m_K\le n-1\) and saturations \(\pi_k=m_k/n\in(0,1)\), deployment action set \(\mathcal A=\mathcal K\), within-cluster assignment space \(\mathcal Z_n=\{0,1\}^n\), exact-count slices \(\mathcal S_k=\{z:\sum_jz_j=m_k\}\) of known cardinality \(M_k=\binom{n}{m_k}\), and the strictly positive cross-label hit matrix \(B_{k\ell}=\Pr\{\operatorname{Bin}(n,\pi_\ell)=m_k\}\). — Process: the whole assignment geometry is finite, so `Z_n := Fin n -> Bool` (Fintype) and `S_k` is a `Finset` slice; `M_k = Nat.choose n m_k` is exactly `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.completeRandomization_card` (Designs/CompleteRandomization.lean:44) after transporting subsets-of-fixed-card to the fixed-count cube. `B_{k l}` is `PMF.binomial_apply` (Mathlib.Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Binomial) read off the coordinate-sum push-forward of `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.bernoulliDesign` with constant per-unit propensity pi_l (Designs/Bernoulli.lean:62). gamma_k / beta_k are the Han target and nominal assignment masses on this same finite space. search trace: grep '^## ' ../doc/API.md -> section 18 (Experimentation); Glob ../Causalean/Experimentation/**/*.lean; grep decls in DesignBased/Designs/{Bernoulli,CompleteRandomization}.lean; leansearch 'probability mass function of binomial distribution equals n choose k times p^k (1-p)^(n-k)' -> PMF.binomial_apply. No Causalean decl packages an exact-count saturation menu with a cross-label hit matrix; define-local.

An unrestricted law \(P\) of a bounded cluster potential-outcome schedule \(Y=(Y_j(z))_{j\le n,z\in\mathcal Z_n}\in[0,1]^{n\times\mathcal Z_n}\), with arbitrary within-cluster interference and no interference across clusters, cluster welfare \(W(z)=n^{-1}\sum_jY_j(z)\), assignment-specific means \(\mu_z=\mathbb E_P[W(z)]\), exact-slice welfare targets \(U_k=M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\mu_z\), calibrated and raw slice variances \(\tau_k^2,b_k^2,\rho_k^2=\tau_k^2+b_k^2\), a bounded target-only loss \(\mathcal L(U,a)\), a regular baseline \(P_0\) with assignment marginals \(P_{0,z}\), its product coupling \(\bar P_0=\bigotimes_zP_{0,z}\), log normalizers \(\Lambda_{z,k}\), the nondegeneracy constant \(\underline\tau\), and the tied-best face \(A=\arg\max_kU_k(P_0)\) with \(|A|\ge2\). — Process: this is the superpopulation half of the hybrid; `[0,1]^(n x Z_n)` is a compact metric space (finite product of unit intervals), which is exactly what the REUSED Mathlib weak-compactness instance `instCompactSpaceProbabilityMeasure` consumes (round-3 revision: no longer a gate, see lem:weak-compactness-compact-laws) — F2 must choose the cube's Lean encoding so that `[CompactSpace]`, `[T2Space]` and `[BorelSpace]` all discharge by instance search. Causalean's `Experimentation/DesignBased/PotentialOutcome.lean` (`ProperlySpecified`, `Yobs`) is the finite-population, fixed-schedule flavour: it makes probability come only from randomization and has no schedule law, so it is surveyed but bypass-justified here (see substrate_survey). `Causalean.PO/` is the measure-theoretic superpopulation framework but is indexed by a scalar treatment, not by a within-cluster assignment vector with arbitrary interference. search trace: grep '^## ' ../doc/API.md -> 8h `PO/`, 18 `Experimentation/`; grep decls DesignBased/PotentialOutcome.lean; leansearch 'set of probability measures on a compact metric space is compact for weak convergence, Prohorov tightness' -> MeasureTheory.instCompactSpaceProbabilityMeasure, IsTightMeasureSet.of_compactSpace. No decl carries a bounded cluster schedule law with per-assignment marginals; define-local.

Exactly one of two mutually exclusive randomization regimes, together with the observed-data laws they induce. In \(\mathsf B(p)\), labels \(L_1,\ldots,L_C\) are i.i.d. \(\operatorname{Categorical}(p)\), \(p\in\Delta_K\) chosen before sampling and possibly on the boundary, and given \(L_c=\ell\) the coordinates of \(Z_c\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_\ell)\); the target-hit rates are \(q=Bp\) and the nominal-label hit rates are \(\eta_k=p_kB_{kk}\). In \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), the label vector is uniform over vectors with fixed counts \(C_{C,k}\) (\(C_{C,k}/C\to\alpha_k\)) and \(Z_c\mid L_c=k\) is uniform on \(\mathcal S_k\). Each regime yields a known Markov kernel (\(R_{B,p}\), \(R^{CR}_{C_C}\)) from schedules to records \(O_c=(L_c,Z_c,(Y_{c,j}(Z_c))_j)\), the observed laws \(Q^B_{P,p}=PR_{B,p}\) and \(Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}=P^{\otimes C}R^{CR}_{C_C}\), the full and reduced experiments \(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{full}}_{C,\cdot}\), \(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{hit}}_{C,\cdot}\) built from the target-hit reduction \(O_c\mapsto O_c^{\mathrm{hit}}\) or label deletion, and the class \(\mathfrak D_C\) of all measurable randomized deployment rules. — Process: both regimes are finite two-stage designs, exactly the shape of `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.compound` (TwoStage.lean) with stage-1 design on the label menu and stage-2 conditional design `bernoulliDesign` (regime B) or `completeRandomization` (regime CR); cross-cluster independence is structural via `prodDesign` (Product.lean), which is also the Lean content of partial interference. The randomization-and-coarsening kernels R and the observed-data laws are the composition of that finite design with the schedule law: `ProbabilityTheory.Kernel` composition, with `Causalean.Stat.kernelMean` / `Causalean.Stat.sqRisk_kernelMean_le_comp` (Stat/Minimax/MarkovKernelTransport.lean) as the risk-transport pattern F3 should adapt for the deletion theorems. search trace: grep '^## ' ../doc/API.md -> 18 (Product/TwoStage combinators), 10z (minimax substrate); grep decls DesignBased/{Product,TwoStage,Designs/*}.lean and Stat/Minimax/MarkovKernelTransport.lean; leansearch 'local asymptotic normality limit experiment Bayes risk lower bound ...' -> ProbabilityTheory.{bayesRisk,avgRisk,bayesRisk_le_avgRisk} (Mathlib.Probability.Decision.Risk.*). Causalean has no two-regime saturation experiment with a target-hit coarsening; define-local over `compound`/`prodDesign`. REVISED (redirect pass 3, statement-shape fix, dependency closure of the two deletion theorems): the rule class `D_C` bound by this block is a class of MARKOV DECISION KERNELS, not of measurable functions into a finite action type. F2 must bind it as `ProbabilityTheory.Kernel Obs Act` with `[MeasurableSpace Act] [StandardBorelSpace Act] [Nonempty Act]` and `IsMarkovKernel`, where `Obs` is the observation space of the invoked experiment (full or reduced, either regime). Two reasons, both structural rather than cosmetic: the core's generality clause explicitly ranges over ALL measurable randomized rules on an ARBITRARY standard-Borel decision space (the finite deployment menu `A = K` and the Han ranking vector are two instances), and the deletion proofs work by COMPOSING a rule with a parameter-free kernel in each direction — the nontarget-outcome simulation kernel F_z^0 of (5)-(6) and the label kernel (7) — which is kernel composition, an operation a bare function-valued rule does not support. The finite-menu instance is recovered by taking `Act = Fin K` with its discrete Borel structure, so no downstream node's conclusion shape changes. `Causalean.Stat.kernelMean` / `sqRisk_kernelMean_le_comp` (Stat/Minimax/MarkovKernelTransport.lean:56,165) remain the technique reference for the composition step, and `ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.comp` supplies the composition itself.

The observed-data statistics of the experiment: cell counts \(N_z\), cell means \(\overline W_z\) (with the prespecified fallback \(1/2\) on \(N_z=0\)), the assignment-calibrated exact-hit estimator \(\widetilde U_{C,k}=M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\overline W_z\) with its full vector \(\widetilde U_C\) and active restriction \(\widetilde U_{C,A}\), the raw pooled-hit estimator \(\widehat U^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,k}\) and the Han--Owusu--Shin estimator \(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}\), the influence functions \(\phi_k^B,\psi_k,\phi_k^{HOS},\phi_k^{nom},\phi_{c,k}^{CR}\), the scores \(\dot\ell_k^B,\dot\ell_{c,k}^{CR}\) and central sequences \(\Delta_C^B,\Delta_C^{CR}\), the information and covariance matrices \(I_B,I_{CR},\Sigma_B^{(K)},\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)},\Sigma_{B,A},\Sigma_{CR,A}\), the calibrated covariance estimators \(\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)},\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\), and the tie-aware rank endpoints \(r_k^\pm(U)\), rank target \(\operatorname{Rank}_k(U)\), and simultaneous rank confidence set \(\mathcal R_{C,k}(\gamma)\). — Process: the calibrated estimator is a Hajek-type cell-ratio statistic. REVISION (round 2, abstraction fix): the `o_P` ratio expansions (13), (18), (20), (24), (68), (75) are split into (i) a PURE ALGEBRA step — `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.ratio_remainder_capped_bound` (RatioLinearization.lean:40), a real-number inequality on `|sn (A/D - mu) - sn^{-1} G| <= 2 |sn^{-1} G| |n^{-1} D - 1|` with no design or measure in its statement, hence transferable verbatim — and (ii) a PROBABILISTIC ABSORPTION step, which is NOT `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.Slutsky`: `finiteDesign_cdf_converging_together` is quantified over `D : forall n, FiniteDesign (Omega n)` (Slutsky.lean:35-36) and `FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb` over the same (InProb.lean:56), neither of which has an instance on a record law with a `[0,1]^n` outcome coordinate. The record-level limit theory does NOT go through the `FiniteDesign` layer. A record `O_c = (L_c, Z_c, (Y_{c,j}(Z_c))_j)` has a continuous outcome coordinate in `[0,1]^n`, so it is not a `Fintype` point of a `FiniteDesign`; `FiniteDesign.chebyshev` and `IndepSummandsCLT` do not typecheck against it. Concentration over the iid record law is `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.iid_sum_chebyshev` (IidSums.lean:84, stated for `Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin N => mu)`), the Bernoulli joint CLT is `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample.clt_normalizedSum_vec` (GaussianLimit.lean:116), the CR label-conditional triangular-array CLT is `Causalean.SteinMethod.bounded_degree_dependency_clt` (StandardizedDepGraphCLT.lean:185), and the tau_k^2 + b_k^2 split is Mathlib's measure-theoretic law of total variance `ProbabilityTheory.integral_condVar_add_variance_condExp`. The `FiniteDesign` algebra remains in force for the pure randomization layer (Z_c given L_c on the finite cube), which is where lem:exact-hit-factorization lives. The studentized max-t inversion is likewise re-routed: `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.WaldCoverage.conservative_wald_liminf_of_studentized_cdf` (WaldCoverage.lean:45-46) and the design-side `DesignBased.GaussianCDF` wrapper it consumes are both `FiniteDesign`-quantified, so they are analogous-technique references only (single contrast under a finite design, gap: all K(K-1)/2 studentized pairs under a record law); the inversion is built from `Causalean.Stat.Tendsto_dist_vec.map_continuous` (ConvergenceVec.lean:245) for the continuous max-t functional plus `Causalean.Mathlib.stdNormalCDF` (+`stdNormalCDF_continuous`, `stdNormalCDF_strictMono`, `probit`) for continuity and inversion of the limiting quantile. search trace: grep '^## ' ../doc/API.md -> 18 (Chebyshev/GaussianCDF/Wald block, now bypass-justified), 12 (Stat CLT/Concentration/Limit); grep 'clt_normalizedSum_vec|bounded_degree_dependency_clt|iid_sum_chebyshev' ../Causalean -> Stat/CLT/GaussianLimit.lean:116, Mathlib/Probability/SteinMethod/StandardizedDepGraphCLT.lean:185, Stat/Concentration/Matrix/IidSums.lean:84; grep 'add_isLittleOp_one|Tendsto_dist_vec|IsAsymLinearVec' ../Causalean -> Stat/Limit/ConvergenceVec.lean:58,84,222,245, Stat/Limit/Convergence.lean:90,174, Stat/CLT/AsymptoticLinearity.lean:237,409, Stat/CLT/AsymptoticLinearityVec.lean:179 (all namespace `Causalean.Stat`, all stated for a generic probability measure); leansearch 'law of total variance: variance equals expectation of conditional variance plus variance of conditional expectation' -> ProbabilityTheory.integral_condVar_add_variance_condExp (Mathlib.Probability.CondVar). REVISED (redirect pass 3, statement-shape fix, dependency closure of the estimator and CR nodes): three bindings in this block get an explicit guard or witness, because the objects are otherwise undefined or unwitnessed at the shapes the statements use. (1) POSITIVE LABEL MASS. The exact-count influence coordinate `phi^CR_{c,k}(O_c) = (C/C_{C,k}) 1{L_c = k} {W(Z_c) - mu_{Z_c}}` and the exact-count score `dot-ell^CR_{c,k}` divide by the realized stratum count, and the stratum-conditional centering `E[W(Z_c) | L_c = k] = U_k` conditions on an event of probability `C_{C,k}/C`. F2 must therefore carry `0 < C_{C,k}` as a side condition on exactly the coordinates `k` for which these objects are formed (or define them by the prespecified fallback off that event and state every identity on `{k : 0 < C_{C,k}}`), never as a global unstated convention. On the active face this is supplied eventually by ass:cr-shares and on the full menu by ass:cr-all-shares, so it introduces no new assumption node and no `hyps` change; it is a well-definedness guard inside the statements. The same guard applies to the CR half of `hatSigma_C^{(K)}` and `hatSigma_{C,A}`, whose diagonal entries carry the factor `C/C_{C,k}^2`. (2) ASYMPTOTIC-LINEARITY WITNESSES. The asymptotic variances asserted for `U^HOS_{C,k}`, the raw pooled estimator and the nominal-label efficient procedure are not free-standing reals: F2 emits one shared witness predicate in `Helpers/Estimators.lean` — the scalar `Causalean.Stat.IsAsymLinear` (Stat/CLT/AsymptoticLinearity.lean) and its vector form `IsAsymLinearVec` (AsymptoticLinearityVec.lean:179) — and every AVAR claim in this world is stated as `IsAsymLinear <estimator> <influence coordinate>` together with the variance of that coordinate, so the number is always attached to an exhibited influence function. (3) RANK LEVEL. `R_{C,k}(gamma)` is only defined for `0 < gamma < 1` (its max-t critical value is `probit` at a level in the open unit interval, `Causalean.Mathlib.probit` / `stdNormalCDF_probit`), so the level is a bundled hypothesis of the constructor rather than a bare real; see def:rank-target-and-set.

The local Gaussian decision problem the mechanism comparison is priced in. On a tied-best face \(A\) with \(|A|\ge2\), local welfare displacements \(h\in\mathbb R^A\) act only through the translation quotient \(H_A=\mathbb R^A/\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_A\}\), observed through the reference contrast matrix \(D_A\) with quotient norm \(\lVert[h]\rVert_A=\lVert D_Ah\rVert_2\) and radius \(M\). For positive variance and rate vectors \(v_A,r_A\), \(X\sim N\{h,\Sigma(v_A,r_A)\}\) with \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(v_k/r_k)\) and quotient covariance \(\Omega_A=D_A\Sigma D_A'\); \(G_A(v_A,r_A)\) is the minimax simple-regret value over all measurable randomized selectors (lower-semicontinuous closure at boundary rates) and \(G_{A,M}\) its compact-quotient restriction. The least-favourable exponential-tilt path \(P_{t,h,z}\), \(\bar P_{t,h}\), \(\bar P_{C,h}=\bar P_{C^{-1/2},h}\) realizes these displacements; \(\Phi\) and \(\varphi\) are the standard normal distribution function and density, \(\kappa=\max_{x\ge0}x\Phi(-x)\); \(R^\star_{B,A}\) and \(R^\star_{CR,A}\) are the optimized face values over the Bernoulli hit polytope \(B\Delta_K\) (with \(s_A(p)\), \(a_A(p)\), \(s_{A,\max}\)) and over \(\Delta_A\); \(t,F_v(t),t^\star\) are the two-policy allocation coordinates; \(\varepsilon,\delta_{\varepsilon,A},L_\varepsilon,U_\varepsilon,\mathfrak C_K\) are the validated-certificate objects; and \(C_B,C_{CR}\) are the two cluster budgets compared at equal leading local regret. — Process: `G_A` is an instance of `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue` (Stat/Minimax/MinimaxValue.lean:62) with estimator type = measurable randomized selectors and parameter type = R^A; `Causalean.Stat.le_minimaxValue_of_two_point` (line 161) is precisely the two-point lower bound used for kappa in thm:two-policy-minimax and lem:gaussian-information-order (32), and `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue_le_minimaxValue` / `minimaxValue_le_worstCaseRisk` give the comparison and upper-bound halves. Phi and phi are `Causalean.Mathlib.stdNormalCDF` / `stdNormalPDF` with `stdNormalCDF_neg`, `stdNormalCDF_continuous`. The finite-prior Bayes machinery for the compact certificate is the FINITE-ACTION, FINITE-PARAMETER layer over a CONTINUUM observation (REVISED round 7, superseding the round-5 wording): `Causalean.Stat.finiteDesignBayesRisk` (Stat/Minimax/FiniteKernelBayes.lean:280) for the Bayes value `iInf a, D.E (loss a)` under the simple-regret loss `A -> S -> R` and `Causalean.Stat.finiteDesignBayesRisk_le_minimaxValue` (line 287) for Bayes <= `minimaxValue` (the same carrier as G_A above, so the lower certificate chains without a change of vocabulary). Both constrain only the STATE type (FiniteKernelBayes.lean:26-27, `[Fintype S] [Nonempty S] [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSingletonClass S]`), which is instantiated here by the finite rational PARAMETER GRID on the quotient ball, and impose nothing on the observation space, so they apply verbatim to this world. WHICH ACTION TYPE (REVISED round 8, static-Bayes-misuse fix — the observation-freeness just noted is what makes this choice load-bearing rather than incidental): because that loss has NO observation argument, the action type is the only slot through which a selector can enter, and the two layers must be kept apart. (i) At action type = the face's POLICY MENU `A`, `finiteDesignBayesRisk` names the pointwise posterior minimum `min_a c a y` of the certificate's integrand; its companion inequality then reads against the STATIC-ACTION value `iInf_a sSup_s loss a s`, which is NOT `G_{A,M}` — applying it pointwise in `y` and integrating is a type mismatch, not a proof step, and is the defect this round retires. (ii) At action type = `Sel`, the SUBTYPE of measurable randomized quotient selectors `delta : R^(|A|-1) -> Delta_A` — which is precisely the estimator type at which this block spells `G_A` and `G_{A,M}` as `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue` — `finiteDesignBayesRisk_le_minimaxValue` is invoked ONCE, on the finite rational parameter grid, and lands at the finite-grid selector minimax value; the remaining gap to the full quotient ball is a MODEL-CLASS comparison, `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue_mono_class_of_nonneg` (MinimaxValue.lean:235, same estimator type, an embedding of the grid into `K_M`, nonnegative risks and `BddAbove` per selector), with `minimaxValue_subtype_eq_sInf_worstCaseRisk` (266) available if F3 prefers to spell the selector class by a predicate rather than a subtype. That two-layer route is written out in the auxiliaries `lem:finite-action-posterior-cost` (layer (i), the integrand and its Tonelli integral) and `lem:selector-grid-bayes-minimax-bridge` (layer (ii), the single minimax application and the model-class step). The whole of `Causalean.Stat.Minimax.FinitePosteriorBayesRisk` is now BYPASSED, for two independent reasons: its decision layer (`posteriorMean`:174, `posteriorMean_minimizes`:278, `iInf_squaredRisk_eq_posteriorResidual`:287, `finiteDesignBayesRisk_statewiseSquaredLoss`:328) is an infimum over real-valued estimators `T : X -> R` under `squaredRisk`, whereas this world's selectors pick one action from the finite policy menu under simple regret (round-5 finding); and its loss-free disintegration layer (`kernelMass`:37, `observationMass`:77, `posteriorWeight`:98, `observationMass_mul_posteriorWeight`:142) is declared under `[Fintype X] [MeasurableSingletonClass X]` and built from SINGLETON observation masses `(L s).real {x}`, whereas this world's observation is the continuum quotient Gaussian `Y ~ N(D_A h, Omega_A)` on `R^(|A|-1)`, on which every singleton is null and the guarded weight is identically zero (round-7 finding). The posterior cost `c_a(y)` of the certificate is therefore a DENSITY object: `Y` is carried by whitening with `Omega_A^(-1/2)` into a `Measure.pi` of `ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1`, its density is a finite product of `ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDF` factors (`gaussianReal_of_var_ne_zero`, `rnDeriv_gaussianReal`, `gaussianPDF_pos`), and the posterior weights are the density ratios, built locally in `lem:finite-action-posterior-cost`. [MeasurableSingletonClass X]` and the singleton-mass chain kernelMass:37 / observationMass:77 / posteriorWeight:98 / observationMass_mul_posteriorWeight:142, confirming the finite-observation restriction; Read ../Causalean/Stat/Minimax/FiniteKernelBayes.lean:26-27,276-296 -> only S is Fintype-constrained, the observation space is unconstrained, so finiteDesignBayesRisk / finiteDesignBayesRisk_le_minimaxValue are kept; grep 'posterior|rnDeriv|withDensity' ../Causalean/Stat -> 21 files, of which the posterior ones (Minimax/FiniteSquaredLoss/PosteriorBarycenter.lean, FiniteRaoBlackwell/Posterior.lean) are again finite-observation (`[Fintype (X b)]`) and squared-loss, so no Causalean density-posterior fit exists. nl.statement: Set \(\bar P_0=\bigotimes_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}P_{0,z}\). Define \(\bar P_{t,h}=\bigotimes_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}P_{t,h,z}\) and \(\bar P_{C,h}=\bar P_{C^{-1/2},h}\).  The decision-relevant coordinate of \(h\) is its class \([h]\in H_A=\mathbb R^A/\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_A\}\), but the statistical path retains the common-shift nuisance rather than fixing a representative.

nl.statement:
Fix \(a_0=\min A\), let \(D_A\) have rows \(e_k^{\prime}-e_{a_0}^{\prime}\), \(k\in A\setminus\{a_0\}\), and put \(H_A=\mathbb R^A/\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_A\}\) and \(\lVert[h]\rVert_A=\lVert D_Ah\rVert_2\).  For positive \(v_A,r_A\), let \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)=\operatorname{diag}(v_k/r_k:k\in A)\) and \(\Omega_A=D_A\Sigma(v_A,r_A)D_A^{\prime}\), and define
\[
G_A(v_A,r_A)=\inf_{\delta}\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A}\mathbb E_h\!\left[\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_{\delta(X)}\right],\qquad X\mid h\sim N\{h,\Sigma(v_A,r_A)\},
\]
where the infimum is over all measurable randomized selectors.  Equivalently the infimum is over location-invariant selectors \(\delta(x+c\mathbf 1_A)=\delta(x)\), hence over selectors based on \(D_AX\sim N(D_Ah,\Omega_A)\).  For \(M<\infty\), \(G_{A,M}(v_A,r_A)\) is the same invariant-selector game with \(\lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M\).  On \([0,\infty)^A\), define \(G_A\) at a boundary rate as the lower-semicontinuous closure \(\liminf_{r'\to r,\ r'>0}G_A(v_A,r')\).

review.note: On the stated GaussianFaceDomain, the two components are the full and compact simple-regret minimax values; gaussian_quotient_reduction supplies equality with invariant quotient selectors, while gaussian_information_order identifies action-relevant zero-rate boundaries with top, agreeing with the lower-semicontinuous closure.

nl.statement:
Using the lower-semicontinuous boundary value of \(G_A\), define
\[
R_{B,A}^\star(v_A)=\min_{p\in\Delta_K}G_A(v_A,(Bp)_A),\qquad
R_{CR,A}^\star(v_A)=\min_{a\in\Delta_A}G_A(v_A,a).
\]
Only the active coordinates are supplied to \(G_A\).  Positivity of every entry of \(B\) keeps \((Bp)_A\) in the positive orthant, whereas boundary coercivity makes every minimizer in the exact-count simplex belong to \(\Delta_A^\circ\); allocating mass to inactive exact-count policies is therefore excluded after the active face is selected.

review.note: Positive entries of B make Lean's Bernoulli positivity clause redundant, while boundary coercivity makes the open active-simplex sInf equal the paper's attained closed-simplex minimum; only active coordinates affect the equivalent Gaussian game.

nl.statement:

\[
F_v(t)=\frac{v_1}{q_1(t)}+\frac{v_2}{q_2(t)},\qquad
t^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{0\leq t\leq1}F_v(t).
\]
This is the exact contrast-variance allocation map for the two-action quotient game.  Its exact-count counterpart minimizes \(v_1/\alpha_1+v_2/(1-\alpha_1)\) over \(0<\alpha_1<1\).

review.note: The unfolded objective has exactly the stated q1 and q2 denominators; on the positive-variance hit-matrix domain its minimizer is unique, so the leftmost-minimizer sInf equals argmin, and the displayed square-root share is the exact-count minimizer.

Solve each finite parameter game by a rational finite prior and a represented randomized selector; evaluate posterior cost functions and selector risks by directed interval arithmetic; and add explicit parameter-grid, covariance-Kullback--Leibler, observation-tail, quadrature, and ambiguous-action-cell errors. Choose \(0<\lambda<1\); split a Gaussian observation into independent screening and decision observations with covariances \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)/\lambda\) and \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)/(1-\lambda)\); retain arms within threshold \(T\) of the screening maximum; multiply the decision observation by \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\); and apply the compact quotient certificate separately on every realized nonempty subset \(S\subseteq A\). nl.statement:
For every fixed \(C\), \(p\), and bounded target-only loss \(\mathcal L\), regime \(\mathsf B(p)\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{full}}(p)))]
=
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{hit}}(p)))].
\]
The equality persists after deleting \(L_c\) conditional on every realized target assignment.  More generally, the same equality holds when the displayed finite deployment action space and its rule class are replaced by any standard-Borel decision space and all measurable randomized rules, provided the loss is bounded and depends on the schedule law only through \(U\).  This includes the ranking action of Han--Owusu--Shin.  It holds for rules observing the entire outcome vector because the reverse inequality fixes every nontarget assignment marginal at a known distribution and replaces the unidentified schedule coupling by the product of its assignment-specific marginals.

review.note: After unfolding the risk, experiment, loss, hit-reduction, and label-deletion definitions, Lean states the finite-action equality, its arbitrary standard-Borel-action extension, and equality after deleting labels; the four additional conjuncts are unconditional measurability facts and do not strengthen the claim.

nl.statement:

\[

=
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{hit}}(\alpha)))].
\]
More generally, the equality holds after replacing the displayed finite deployment action space and its rule class by any standard-Borel decision space and all measurable randomized rules, provided the loss is bounded and target-only; this includes the ranking action of Han--Owusu--Shin.  Here the reduced experiment deletes the randomized label vector after the realized exact-count assignments are recorded.

review.note: After unfolding, the two CR experiments are the full fixed-count observed law and its coordinatewise label-deleted image retaining each exact-count assignment and outcome; both minimax functionals range over all bounded schedule laws and all measurable randomized finite-action or standard-Borel rules with the exact-slice welfare target and bounded nonnegative target-only loss.

The full calibrated vector satisfies \[\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_B^{(K)}),\qquad \widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_B^{(K)}.\] Its active restriction has covariance \(\Sigma_{B,A}=(\Sigma_B^{(K)})_{AA}\).

nl.statement: Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\) with \(\alpha_k>0\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), the full calibrated vector satisfies \[\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}),\qquad \widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}.\] Conditionally on the fixed-count label vector, its triangular-array influence coordinates are \(\phi_{c,k}^{CR}\).

nl.statement: Fix \(k\) with \(p_k>0\), and write \(\eta_k=p_kB_{kk}\). Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1) is exactly \[\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}=\frac{1}{Cp_k}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{L_c=k\}\frac{\gamma_k(Z_c)}{\beta_k(Z_c)}W_c(Z_c)=\frac{1}{C\eta_k}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{L_c=k,Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}W_c(Z_c).\] It has influence function \(\phi_k^{HOS}=\eta_k^{-1}\mathbf 1\{L=k,Z\in\mathcal S_k\}W(Z)-U_k\) and \[\operatorname{AVAR}(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k})=\frac{\tau_k^2+b_k^2}{\eta_k}+U_k^2\left(\frac1{\eta_k}-1\right).\] The best regular estimator in the nominal-label-\(k\) subexperiment has canonical gradient \(\phi_k^{nom}\) and efficiency bound \(\tau_k^2/\eta_k\). Therefore, whenever \(q_k>\eta_k\) and \(\tau_k^2>0\), \[\frac{\tau_k^2}{q_k}<\frac{\tau_k^2}{p_kB_{kk}}\leq\operatorname{AVAR}(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}).\] If \(b_k^2>0\), assignment-cell calibration within the nominal subexperiment is itself strictly more efficient than Eq. (S1), apart from the additional Horvitz--Thompson participation term displayed above.

review.note: After unfolding all referenced definitions, Lean encodes the same HOS identity, influence function, exact variance, nominal canonical gradient and efficiency bound, attainment by assignment-cell calibration, and both strict-refinement comparisons; the displayed weak inequality follows from the variance identity, 0 < eta ≤ 1, and nonnegativity of b² and U².

It is efficient if and only if \(b_k^2=0\). At \(n=4\), count-one assignment means \((4/5,4/5,1/5,1/5)\) give \(U_1=1/2\), \(\tau_1^2=4/25\), \(\rho_1^2=1/4\), and excess \(9/100\) before division by \(q_1\).

nl.statement:
Let \(A=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_kU_k(P_0)\), with \(|A|\geq2\), and suppose every policy in \(A^c\) is separated below the tied active welfare.  For every representative \(h\in\mathbb R^A\), including its common-shift component, the path \(\bar P_{C,h}=\bar P_{C^{-1/2},h}\) satisfies \(Q^B_{\bar P_0,p}=Q^B_{P_0,p}\), \(dU_k(\bar P_{t,h})/dt|_{t=0}=h_k\), and
\[
\log\frac{d(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}{d(Q^B_{P_0,p})^{\otimes C}}
=h^{\prime}\Delta_C^B-\frac12h^{\prime}I_Bh+o_{(Q^B_{P_0,p})^{\otimes C}}(1),
\qquad \Delta_C^B\Rightarrow N(0,I_B),
\]
with \(\dot\ell_k^B\in L^2_0(Q^B_{P_0,p})\) and \(I_B=\operatorname{diag}(q_k/\tau_k^2:k\in A)\).  Under \(\bar P_{C,h}\),
\[
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}\Rightarrow
N\{h,\Sigma_{B,A}\}.
\]
For every measurable randomized rule sequence \(\delta_C\) and every \(M<\infty\),
\[
\liminf_{C\to\infty}\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A:\ \lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M}
\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}
\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]
\geq G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,q_A).
\]
Moreover \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\) as \(M\to\infty\).  The same lower bounds hold for rules observing the full Bernoulli experiment by nuisance deletion.

review.note: Unfolding the path, observed law, LAN, Gaussian-shift, rule, regret, quotient-norm, and Gaussian-value definitions gives the stated baseline equivalence, active derivatives, score CLT/LAN expansion, shifted estimator limit, and full-record all-rule compact lower bound; compact values are definitionally nondecreasing in the real radius and their natural-radius Tendsto is the equivalent cofinal formulation of G_{A,M} ↑ G_A.

nl.statement:
Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), for every representative \(h\in\mathbb R^A\), including its common-shift component, the product-coupled path satisfies \(Q^{CR}_{\bar P_0,C_C}=Q^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}\) and
\[
\log\frac{dQ^{CR}_{\bar P_{C,h},C_C}}{dQ^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}}
=h^{\prime}\Delta_C^{CR}-\frac12h^{\prime}I_{CR}h+o_{Q^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}}(1),
\qquad \Delta_C^{CR}\Rightarrow N(0,I_{CR}),
\]
where, conditionally on the fixed-count label vector, \(\dot\ell_{c,k}^{CR}\) is centered in its stratum and \(I_{CR}=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_k/\tau_k^2:k\in A)\).  Under \(\bar P_{C,h}\),
\[
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N\{h,\Sigma_{CR,A}\}.
\]
For every measurable randomized rule sequence \(\delta_C\) and every \(M<\infty\),
\[
\liminf_{C\to\infty}\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A:\ \lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M}
\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{Q^{CR}_{\bar P_{C,h},C_C}}
\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]
\geq G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,\alpha_A),
\]
and \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\).  The independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) target-bit submodel has \(\tau_k^2=1/4\) and information \(4\alpha_k\); it is a witness, not a restriction on the general path.

review.note: After unfolding the path, CR observed law, score, LAN, Gaussian-shift, randomized-rule, regret, quotient-norm, and Gaussian-value definitions, Lean equivalently states baseline observational equality, LAN and score convergence for every full active representative including common shifts, the shifted estimator limit, the all-rule compact local-regret lower bound, the cofinal monotone convergence G_{A,M} ↑ G_A, and the independent fair target-bit witness.

nl.statement:
When \(K=2\) and \(A=\mathcal K\), the quotient statistic is \(X_1-X_2\), and for positive rates
\[
G_A(v_A,r_A)=\kappa\sqrt{\frac{v_1}{r_1}+\frac{v_2}{r_2}},
\]
attained by selecting policy one exactly when \(X_1-X_2\geq0\).  Consequently the optimized exact-count share is
\[
\alpha_1^\star=\frac{\sqrt{v_1}}{\sqrt{v_1}+\sqrt{v_2}}.
\]
For Bernoulli labels, \(t^\star\) minimizes \(F_v(t)\).  If \(B_{11}>B_{12}\) and \(B_{22}>B_{21}\), then \(t^\star=0\) exactly when
\[
\frac{v_1}{v_2}\leq\frac{(B_{22}-B_{21})B_{12}^2}{(B_{11}-B_{12})B_{22}^2},
\]
and \(t^\star=1\) exactly when
\[
\frac{v_1}{v_2}\geq\frac{(B_{22}-B_{21})B_{11}^2}{(B_{11}-B_{12})B_{21}^2};
\]
otherwise it is the unique interior value
\[
t^\star=
\frac{B_{22}\sqrt{v_1(B_{11}-B_{12})/[v_2(B_{22}-B_{21})]}-B_{12}}
{(B_{11}-B_{12})+(B_{22}-B_{21})\sqrt{v_1(B_{11}-B_{12})/[v_2(B_{22}-B_{21})]}}.
\]
For \(n=4\), \((\pi_1,\pi_2)=(1/4,1/2)\), and \(v_1=v_2\),
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}27/64&1/4\\27/128&3/8\end{pmatrix},\qquad
t^\star=-80+\frac{288\sqrt{462}}{77}.
\]
Relative to optimized exact-count assignment, the exact regret ratio and cluster-count ratio are, respectively,
\[
\left(\frac{43}{54}+\frac{\sqrt{462}}{27}\right)^{1/2}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{43}{54}+\frac{\sqrt{462}}{27}.
\]
They lie in \([1.26189430296,1.26189430298]\) and \([1.59237723185,1.59237723187]\), while \(t^\star\in[0.39383577842,0.39383577844]\).

L_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)\leq G_{A,M}(v_A,r_A)\leq U_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A),
\qquad U_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)-L_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)\leq\varepsilon.
\]
Every certificate has a complete machine-checkable transcript containing the rational inputs, parameter, observation, and covariance branch cells, working precision, all directed enclosures, the error-budget decomposition, the checker code revision, and a checksum.  Since every entry of \(B\) is positive, finitely many such compact cells cover the Bernoulli outer polytope \((B\Delta_K)_A\); for exact-count designs the same conclusion holds on each compact subset of \(\Delta_A^\circ\), but not uniformly up to its boundary.  For \(n=6\), \(A=\mathcal K\), and \((m_1,m_2,m_3)=(1,2,4)\), exact arithmetic gives
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}3125/7776&64/243&4/243\\3125/15552&80/243&20/243\\125/15552&20/243&80/243\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its column sums are \(2375/3888\), \(164/243\), and \(104/243\); hence column two is uniquely maximum-mass and its normalized active vector is \((16/41,20/41,5/41)\).  The certified inequalities in this theorem are the compact fixed-face components used by the hierarchical noncompact and outer-simplex computation.

nl.statement:
Fix \(A\), \(M<\infty\), and a compact representative set \(\mathscr H_{A,M}\subseteq\mathbb R^A\) satisfying
\[
\{[h]:h\in\mathscr H_{A,M}\}
=\{[g]\in H_A:\lVert[g]\rVert_A\leq M\}.
\]
Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), use an independent pilot of size \(m_C\to\infty\) with \(m_C/C\to0\) to estimate \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\), snap it outward to a prespecified rational covariance partition, compute the corresponding compact certificate selector \(\delta_{\varepsilon,A}\), and apply that selector to the calibrated estimator from the remaining clusters.  Uniformly over \(p\in\Delta_K\) and \(h\in\mathscr H_{A,M}\),
\[
\limsup_{C\to\infty}\left\{\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}
\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_{\varepsilon,A}}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]
-U_\varepsilon(v_A,(Bp)_A)\right\}\leq0.
\]
There is a diagonal choice \(\varepsilon_C\downarrow0\), with pilot fraction still vanishing and pilot size diverging, whose Gaussian risk converges uniformly over \(p\in\Delta_K\) to the full-ball value \(G_{A,M}(v_A,(Bp)_A)\).  The equality of quotient images above and Gaussian quotient factorization identify the supremum over \(\mathscr H_{A,M}\) with the supremum over the entire closed quotient radius-\(M\) ball.  The uniformity over \(p\) uses the primitive bound \(\min_{p\in\Delta_K}(Bp)_k=\min_{\ell\in\mathcal K}B_{k\ell}>0\) for every active \(k\).  When this result is invoked in the hierarchical construction, it holds simultaneously over the finitely many retained subsets \(S\subseteq A\), provided the representative set used for each non-singleton \(S\) covers its entire closed quotient ball at the invoked radius; the singleton quotient is trivial.  Global adaptation over every candidate policy is obtained by taking \(A=\mathcal K\), for which Bernoulli positivity supplies positive information for every candidate.

\[

\[

\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_{\varepsilon,A}}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]

nl.statement:
For positive \(v_A,r_A\), \(s>0\), and \(r'_A\geq r_A\) coordinatewise,
\[
G_A(v_A,sr_A)=s^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A),\qquad G_A(v_A,r'_A)\leq G_A(v_A,r_A).
\]
If \((1-\xi)r_A\leq r'_A\leq(1+\xi)r_A\) with \(0<\xi<1\), then
\[
(1+\xi)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A)\leq G_A(v_A,r'_A)\leq(1-\xi)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A).
\]
The positive-rate value is finite and strictly positive.  Under the lower-semicontinuous boundary definition, if any action-relevant coordinate \(r_i\) is zero, then \(G_A(v_A,r_A)=+\infty\).

nl.statement:
Let \(A\) be finite with \(d=|A|\geq2\), let \(v_i,r_i>0\), and write
\[
\Sigma=\Sigma(v_A,r_A)=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i^2:i\in A),
\qquad \sigma_i^2=v_i/r_i,
\qquad \bar\sigma=\max_{i\in A}\sigma_i.
\]
For every nonempty \(S\subseteq A\), let \(G_{S,M}(v_S,r_S)\) denote the compact quotient game obtained by restricting the Gaussian face-game definition to \(S\), with the singleton value set equal to zero.  Fix \(0<\lambda<1\), \(T>0\), and for every nonempty \(S\subseteq A\) choose \(M_S\) satisfying
\[
M_S\geq2\sqrt{1-\lambda}\,T\sqrt{|S|-1},
\qquad
H_{\lambda,T}(v_A,r_A)=\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq A}G_{S,M_S}(v_S,r_S),
\qquad
a_\lambda=\sqrt{2/\lambda}\,\bar\sigma.
\]
If, for each \(S\), a represented invariant selector has risk at most \(G_{S,M_S}(v_S,r_S)+\eta\) on its displayed compact quotient ball, then an explicit randomized invariant selector in the unbounded \(A\)-arm experiment satisfies
\[
H_{\lambda,T}(v_A,r_A)
\leq G_A(v_A,r_A)
\leq \sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A}\mathbb E_h\!\left[\max_{i\in A}h_i-h_{\delta(X)}\right]
\leq
(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\{H_{\lambda,T}(v_A,r_A)+\eta\}
+\frac{2d^2a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \exp\!\left\{-\frac{T^2}{2a_\lambda^2}\right\}.
\]
The construction and bound hold uniformly on every compact cell of positive diagonal variances and simultaneously over the finitely many retained subsets \(S\subseteq A\).  This is adaptation within the declared face \(A\); adaptation over every candidate policy requires applying the construction with \(A=\mathcal K\) and positive information for every candidate.  In particular, for every nonempty \(S\subseteq A\),
\[
G_S(v_S,r_S)\leq G_A(v_A,r_A).
\]

nl.statement:
Let \(\Theta\) and \(\mathcal D\) be nonempty finite sets and let \(d\geq1\) be an integer.  Define the action simplex by \(\Delta_{\mathcal D}=\{v\in[0,1]^{\mathcal D}:\sum_{a\in\mathcal D}v_a=1\}\), and let \(\varpi=(\varpi_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}\) be a probability mass function.  For each positive integer \(C\), let \(\mathsf E_C=(\mathsf X_C,\mathcal F_C,\{P_{C,\theta}:\theta\in\Theta\})\) be an experiment whose laws are all dominated by a reference probability measure \(P_{C,0}\) on \((\mathsf X_C,\mathcal F_C)\), and write \(L_{C,\theta}=dP_{C,\theta}/dP_{C,0}\).  Let the limit experiment be a Gaussian-shift experiment on \(\mathbb R^d\), with canonical observation \(G\), laws \(Q_\theta\) all dominated by a reference law \(Q_0\), and likelihood ratios \(L_\theta(G)=dQ_\theta/dQ_0(G)\).  Suppose that: (i) there are measurable statistics \(T_C\colon\mathsf X_C\to\mathbb R^d\) such that, under \(P_{C,0}\),
\[
 \bigl(T_C,(L_{C,\theta})_{\theta\in\Theta}\bigr)
 \ \rightsquigarrow\ 
 \bigl(G,(L_\theta(G))_{\theta\in\Theta}\bigr),
 \qquad G\sim Q_0;
\]
(ii) every likelihood-ratio sequence is uniformly integrable, in the explicit sense that
\[
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_C
 \mathbb E_{P_{C,0}}\!\left[L_{C,\theta}
 \mathbf 1\{L_{C,\theta}>R\}\right]=0
 \quad\text{for every }\theta\in\Theta;
\]
and (iii) nonnegative losses \(\ell_C(\theta,a)\) and \(\ell(\theta,a)\), indexed by \(\Theta\times\mathcal D\), satisfy
\[
 \max_{\theta\in\Theta,\ a\in\mathcal D}
 |\ell_C(\theta,a)-\ell(\theta,a)|\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sup_{C,\theta,a}\ell_C(\theta,a)<\infty.
\]
For a measurable randomized rule \(\delta_C\colon\mathsf X_C\to\Delta_{\mathcal D}\), define
\[
 \mathcal R_{C,\theta}(\delta_C)
 =\mathbb E_{P_{C,\theta}}\!\left[
   \sum_{a\in\mathcal D}\delta_{C,a}\ell_C(\theta,a)
 \right],
 \qquad
 \mathcal B_C(\delta_C)=\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}\varpi_\theta
 \mathcal R_{C,\theta}(\delta_C).
\]
Then every sequence \((\delta_C)\) obeys
\[
 \liminf_{C\to\infty}\mathcal B_C(\delta_C)
 \ \geq\ 
 \mathcal B_\infty^*(\varpi)
 :=\inf_{\substack{\delta\colon\mathbb R^d\to\Delta_{\mathcal D}\\
                    \delta\ \mathrm{measurable}}}
 \sum_{\theta\in\Theta}\varpi_\theta
 \mathbb E_{Q_\theta}\!\left[
   \sum_{a\in\mathcal D}\delta_a(G)\ell(\theta,a)
 \right].
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \liminf_{C\to\infty}\max_{\theta\in\Theta}
 \mathcal R_{C,\theta}(\delta_C)
 \ \geq\ \mathcal B_\infty^*(\varpi).
\]

nl.statement: The set of Borel probability laws on a compact metric space is compact for the topology of weak convergence.

Let \(C_B,C_{CR}>0\) be cluster budgets for the optimized Bernoulli-label and exact-count designs.  If the Bernoulli design is required to have no larger leading local simple regret than the exact-count design, namely
\[
\frac{R_{B,A}^\star(v_A)}{\sqrt{C_B}}
\leq
\frac{R_{CR,A}^\star(v_A)}{\sqrt{C_{CR}}},
\]
then
\[
\frac{C_B}{C_{CR}}
\geq
\left\{\frac{R_{B,A}^\star(v_A)}{R_{CR,A}^\star(v_A)}\right\}^{2}
\geq\frac1{s_{A,\max}}
\geq\frac1{1-2^{1-n}}.
\]
Equality in the mechanism inequality \(\{R_{B,A}^\star/R_{CR,A}^\star\}^2\geq1/s_{A,\max}\) holds exactly under the support-and-normalized-active-vector criterion in \(\texttt{thm:mechanism-loss}\).

nl.statement:
For every fixed finite \(K\), the routine \(\mathfrak C_K\) gives an arbitrary-\(\varepsilon\) validated certificate in the following extended-value sense.  Fix a declared face \(A\subseteq\mathcal K\) with \(|A|\geq2\) and a compact rational cell of positive \((v_A,r_A)\) on which \(\Omega_A\) is uniformly positive definite.  A deterministic algorithm enumerates every nonempty retained subset \(S\subseteq A\), invokes the compact certificates at explicitly computed radii \(M_S\), and returns a represented randomized selector and outward-rounded numbers satisfying
\[
L^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A}\leq G_A(v_A,r_A)
\leq \sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A}\mathbb E_h\!\left[\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_{\delta(X)}\right]
\leq U^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A},
\qquad U^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A}-L^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A}\leq\varepsilon.
\]
For every retained non-singleton \(S\), the primitive oracle transfer uses a compact representative set \(\mathscr H_{S,M_S}\subseteq\mathbb R^S\) whose quotient classes cover the full closed quotient radius-\(M_S\) ball; the singleton quotient is trivial and uses its exact zero-risk rule.  The routine makes the independent Gaussian split explicit: the screening observation has covariance \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)/\lambda\), the decision observation has covariance \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)/(1-\lambda)\), and the compact selector receives the decision observation multiplied by \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\).  Coordinates within a fixed threshold of the screening maximum are retained.  Hence partial-tie limits such as \((0,-a,-M)\) enter their retained lower-dimensional game rather than an invalid radial truncation.  Uniformity is over retained subsets of this declared face; global adaptation over every candidate policy requires taking \(A=\mathcal K\) with positive information for every candidate.

The same routine certifies both outer designs.  Over \(p\in\Delta_K\), it returns a risk interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\), rational simplex cells containing every minimizer of \(p\mapsto G_A(v_A,(Bp)_A)\), and a feasible \(\varepsilon\)-optimal \(p\).  Over \(a\in\Delta_A\), it returns the analogous objects for \(a\mapsto G_A(v_A,a)\).  A zero action-relevant coordinate has the proved extended value \(+\infty\); a computable two-arm lower bound excludes a whole boundary neighborhood before finite interior branch-and-bound.

For primitive implementation, partition the \(C\) clusters into three disjoint prespecified pieces of sizes \(m_C\), \(N_C^{\mathrm s}\), and \(N_C^{\mathrm d}\), where \(m_C\to\infty\), \(m_C/C\to0\), \(N_C^{\mathrm s}/C\to\lambda\), and \(N_C^{\mathrm d}/C\to1-\lambda\).  Form separate calibrated screening and decision estimators.  Their \(\sqrt C\)-limits have covariances \(\Sigma/\lambda\) and \(\Sigma/(1-\lambda)\), respectively, and the compact selector is applied to \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\) times the decision statistic.  With pilot covariance snapping, the asymptotic scaled simple regret is uniformly bounded by the certified Gaussian upper value over the Bernoulli outer simplex and over each compact active-interior exact-count allocation set.  For every retained non-singleton face \(S\), the face-indexed covering condition identifies the primitive supremum with the full-ball quantity \(G_{S,M_S}\) before the face risks are assembled; the singleton branch remains exact.  The transfer is simultaneous over the finitely many retained subsets of the declared face and over triangular bounded-schedule arrays whose covariance stays in the certified cells.  Fixed-scale inferior policies have vanishing scaled contribution; \(C^{-1/2}\)-scale policies enter the retained compact game.  For global candidate adaptation take \(A=\mathcal K\); under exact counts this also requires all candidate shares in a compact simplex interior.  At a vanishing action-relevant share only \(+\infty\) is asserted.  A diagonal sequence of tolerances, split fractions, pilot sizes, and certificate meshes transfers the certified noncompact Gaussian value and outer design on exactly these domains.
